newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Adsteam Marine share offer to close early.
newsitem.headline: Adsteam Marine share offer to close early.

text.p: Residual Assco Group Ltd, formerly Adelaide Steamship Co Ltd, said on Monday that the share offer for its Adsteam Marine Ltd division was oversubscribed and the offer would close early later on Monday.
The offer had been due to close in the first week of June.
Residual aimed to raise A$160 million (US$123 million) from the sale through the issue of 80 million Adsteam Marine shares at A$2.00 each.

Peter Cottrell, chairman of Residual, said in a statement that the overwhelming demand for Adsteam Marine shares had left directors with no alternative but to close the offers early to ensure a manageable share register.
The offer is underwritten by joint lead managers to the float BZW Australia Ltd and SBC Warburg Australia Ltd.
Adsteam Marine business is represented in more than 30 ports around Australia and the South Pacific region through wholly owned businesses and through joint ventures.
The share offer opened on May 15.

Adsteam Marine said in its prospectus that earnings before interest, tax and abnormals was expected to rise to A$24.4 million in the year to June 30, 1997, compared with A$23 million in the 1995/96 year.
A maximum of 20 percent of the shares would be allocated to Residual Assco shareholders.
Adsteam was one of Australia's largest corporate failures following the debt binge of the 1980s, coming under the control of its bankers in 1990 with debts of A$11 billion.
This has been reduced to less than A$700 million through the sale of its operations.
Sir Ron Brierley's GPG Plc holds a 8.75 percent stake in Residual Assco and Brierley himself is on the company's board.
